candidates.name: HotelRec
candidates.what_it_holds: ~50M TripAdvisor hotel reviews (largest public hotel review corpus), reviews from 2010 onward, global hotels; each record has hotel/user URLs, review date, overall rating, title, full text, and sub-ratings (sleep quality, value, rooms, service, cleanliness, location). Data itself is not committed to the repo -- hosted on a SwitchDrive external link, restricted to academic research use. Introduced in Antognini & Faltings, LREC 2020.
candidates.why_useful: A large, dated, global TripAdvisor review corpus is exactly the raw material for building a review-velocity/review-count demand index (counts of new reviews per hotel per month as an occupancy/nights proxy), addressing gap #2 (realised occupancy proxy) and gap #17 (nowcasting methods) using a non-Airbnb site. Historical depth (2010+) also lets a velocity-vs-known-RevPAR backtest be built further back than our current sources.
candidates.size_hint: ~50M reviews, external download (size unspecified, likely tens of GB)

candidates.name: booking-com-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify-platform scraper for Booking.com: pulls hotel names, star ratings, guest scores, review counts, per-night/gross/net pricing, room availability, per-room rate breakdowns, review text with stay dates/room type/traveler type/owner responses, and forward-looking daily availability + minimum-price calendars. Ships hotels.sample.json and reviews.sample.json examples. MIT licensed, 6 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A working method to pull Booking.com review velocity AND forward availability calendars with realized stay dates -- directly usable for a Booking.com-side review-count demand index and a competitor occupancy/ADR proxy (gaps #2, #9). Left unrun per rules (ToS decision).
candidates.time_coverage: Live pull, forward calendar; historical reviews carry stay dates
candidates.size_hint: On-demand scrape, no bulk data committed beyond samples
candidates.last_activity: recent (Apify actor, actively maintained per repo)

candidates.name: expedia-hotel-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper for guest ratings and review text from Expedia Group brands.
candidates.why_useful: Method to build a review-velocity series for an Expedia-listed competitor supply set, complementing our BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT peer KPI panel with review-count-based demand timing (gap #9).
candidates.last_activity: unknown, part of an active multi-scraper account (factden)

candidates.name: ctrip-trip-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Collects reviews from Trip.com / Ctrip (Chinese OTA).
candidates.why_useful: Only method found touching a Chinese travel platform's review stream -- relevant to APAC demand read-through (gap #7) since ABNB APAC and Chinese outbound travel are otherwise dark to us.

candidates.name: hotels-com-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Gathers ratings and review content from Hotels.com (Expedia Group brand).
candidates.why_useful: Additional non-Airbnb review-velocity source for hotel demand nowcasting cross-checks.

candidates.name: makemytrip-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Collects MakeMyTrip and Goibibo (India) hotel review data.
candidates.why_useful: Only India-specific OTA review scraper found; useful for APAC/India regional travel-demand proxy work (gap #7).

candidates.name: traveloka-hotel-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Extracts Traveloka (Southeast Asia OTA) hotel and activity review data.
candidates.why_useful: Southeast Asia-specific OTA review source, relevant to APAC regional split (gap #7).

candidates.name: tripadvisor-hotel-review-data-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool for extracting TripAdvisor hotel review data (text, ratings, dates).
candidates.why_useful: Alternative TripAdvisor review-pull method to cross-check or refresh review-velocity series beyond HotelRec's 2020 cutoff.

candidates.name: tripadvisor-reviews-scraper (wow4er)
candidates.what_it_holds: Reverse-engineered pure-HTTP TripAdvisor review scraper (mimics Android app / Pixel device fingerprint, no browser). MIT license, updated 2026-08-22.
candidates.why_useful: Actively maintained (as of Aug 2026) low-footprint method for pulling current TripAdvisor reviews with dates -- could refresh a review-velocity series post-2020 where HotelRec stops.

candidates.name: tripadvisor-reviews-scraper (jios325)
candidates.what_it_holds: TripAdvisor hotel reviews scraper using GraphQL API + curl_cffi TLS fingerprinting, no browser automation. MIT license, updated 2026-07-04.
candidates.why_useful: Another actively maintained current-day TripAdvisor review pull method (dated reviews), redundant with wow4er's repo but a second working implementation if one breaks.

candidates.name: google-maps-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: General Google Maps business scraper (3.5k stars, MIT-style/actively maintained): 50+ data points including business emails, phones, socials, ratings and review counts.
candidates.why_useful: Widely used, high-star general-purpose method to pull Google Maps ratings/review-count per business (hotels, STR-adjacent venues) as a demand proxy; also usable for gap #9 (competitor supply counts) by querying hotel/vacation-rental categories by city.

candidates.name: google-maps-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Extracts Google Maps reviews with content, ratings, timestamps, original language + translation, and keyword-filterable review search. MIT license, 31 commits, no sample data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Timestamped Google review pulls are the cleanest 'review velocity' signal available (Google reviews are the largest and most current review pool for lodging businesses) -- directly on-theme for a review-count nowcast built per city/market to compare against Inside Airbnb's own review-based stays index.
candidates.time_coverage: Live pull, current + full historical review timestamps per business

candidates.name: google-reviews-scraper (ScrapingBee)
candidates.what_it_holds: 596-star scalable scraper for Google Maps ratings, review text and business insights.
candidates.why_useful: Second working Google-review-pull implementation (redundant with omkarcloud's) for the same review-velocity use case; higher-star / commercially backed so likely better maintained.

candidates.name: DatafinitiHotelReviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Points to the Datafiniti Hotel Reviews Kaggle dataset (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/datafiniti/hotel-reviews) -- ~35k US hotel reviews with dates, used to build a RAG/fine-tuning knowledge base; repo itself is a pipeline, not the raw CSV.
candidates.why_useful: Points at a smaller, US-focused, dated hotel review dataset (Datafiniti) as an alternative/cross-check source to HotelRec and Kaggle's existing Booking.com 515k set we already hold; marginal incremental value.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: similar in kind to the Booking.com 515k Kaggle set and Portugal hotel-booking dataset we already hold; smaller and US-only

candidates.name: nowcast_lstm
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (R/MATLAB/Julia wrappers) for LSTM-based nowcasting of economic indicator growth rates from mixed-frequency inputs; includes nowcast_lstm_example.zip with a Jupyter notebook and sample datasets; uncertainty intervals, automatic hyperparameter tuning, feature-contribution analysis. MIT license, 90 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made mixed-frequency nowcasting method (alternative to MIDAS/DFM) that could ingest a review-velocity series alongside macro series to nowcast nights/ADR -- directly on-theme for gap #17 (nowcasting methods with mixed-frequency data).

candidates.name: FRBNY Nowcasting
candidates.what_it_holds: New York Fed's dynamic-factor-model nowcasting toolbox (MATLAB/R), the reference implementation behind the NY Fed Nowcast (GDP). 234 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Canonical DFM nowcasting codebase; could be adapted to combine a review-velocity index with macro series into a single nowcast of ABNB nights/GBV, addressing gap #17's DFM method request directly with a proven, citable implementation.

candidates.name: tripadvisor-scraper (gaspa93)
candidates.what_it_holds: General TripAdvisor scraper (8 stars), updated 2026-09-09 (very recent).
candidates.why_useful: Recently active alternative TripAdvisor pull method; unverified scope beyond hotels (may cover attractions/restaurants too).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps other TripAdvisor scrapers listed above

notes: WebSearch's session-wide budget (200/200) was already exhausted before this scout's first query, so no WebSearch calls returned results. DuckDuckGo (html. and lite. endpoints) served CAPTCHA challenges to WebFetch on every attempt -- effectively unusable in this session. Bing search results fetched via WebFetch consistently failed to surface github.com hits for site:github.com queries (returned generic OTA/dictionary/Yelp homepage results instead), suggesting either Bing renders github results below the fold in the markdown conversion or WebFetch's summarizer drops them; plain (non-site-restricted) queries fared no better. What worked: (1) `gh search repos` via the GitHub REST search API -- productive until it hit the shared 5,000/hr rate limit (403) partway through, after which further gh calls returned empty/rate-limited even after a delay; (2) unauthenticated WebFetch against github.com/search?q=...&type=repositories and github.com/topics/<topic> pages, which returned real, well-formed repo lists (topics pages especially reliable) until a 429 kicked in after two consecutive github.com/search calls. Recommend future review-themed scouts lean on github.com/topics/{hotel-reviews,google-reviews,yelp-dataset,web-scraping,tourism} pages first, since they returned clean data even when both search engines and gh were blocked. No committed, ready-to-use CSV/JSON review-velocity dataset with a long multi-year date range was found beyond HotelRec (external host, 2020 cutoff, academic-use-only licence) -- everything else in this theme is scraper/method code (factden's multi-OTA scraper suite, several TripAdvisor and Google Maps scrapers) or generic nowcasting tooling, not a static point-in-time dataset. No repo was found that already computes a 'review velocity as demand nowcast' index end-to-end for hotels/STRs -- that remains a build-it-yourself gap even though the raw pull methods exist.
